Pandey), shareholding, ADB's own 2016–21 evaluation, Japanese ODA as the bilateral comparator, and the narratives about AIIB lending during the 2020 border crisis. It leaves out World Bank and bilateral (non-Japan) lending, the contracts the loans paid for, loan-agreement pricing (not public on project pages), and PIB signing releases (blocked here).

narratives.claim: The Modi government borrowed ₹9,200 crore from a "China-controlled" bank (AIIB) in May–June 2020 while Indian soldiers were killed at Galwan.
narratives.strongestCase: The borrowing is documented: AIIB US$500m health loan (signed 2020-05-08 per FPJ) and US$750m CARES (approved 2020-06-16, signed 2020-06-19, three days after the 15 June clash). China holds ~26.5% of AIIB votes and hosts the bank in Beijing; its president Jin Liqun said publicly he faced "pressure at home" to cut India lending.
narratives.strongestCounter: Both loans were co-financed with ADB (US$1.5bn CARES) and the World Bank under the lead cofinancier's policies; India is AIIB's second-largest shareholder (~7.6%) and had a Vice-President (Pandian) heading its investment pipeline; the money is multilateral capital, not Chinese state finance, and the same programme was signed with ADB on 2020-04-28. A government official told Mint (quoted by the Diplomat): "We are not taking money from China but from the multilateral development bank."
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Evidence that AIIB imposed conditions distinct from ADB's, or that Chinese officials influenced the India loans; or, in the other direction, DEA records showing the loans were requested by India before the CRF window and merely fell on those dates.

symmetryCheck: UPA vs NDA (Union): AIIB did not exist before 2016, so the control is impossible for AIIB by construction; for ADB, the only period totals opened here are NDA-era (US$3bn 2018 "highest since 1986", US$3.9bn 2020, US$4.6bn 2021, US$2.6bn 2023) — UPA-era annual commitments were not fetched, so no Union-level comparison is made and the 2018–21 records are recorded as facts, not as a finding about the government. States: the same lens on ADB's top recipients returns MP (BJP), Rajasthan (INC 2018–23) and Bihar (JD(U)-BJP; MGB 2022–24) and ADB's own explanation (40–50% lower-income-state rule since CPS 2013–17); the AIIB list spans BJP-, INC-, DMK-, LDF-, TMC-, AAP- and YSRCP-run states. The lens produces no partisan picture at this resolution — which is a finding about the lens (state income category predicts lending; party does not, unnormalised). Chinese official finance vs Japanese ODA: China lends to India through AIIB only (no bilateral sovereign loans recorded here); Japan lends bilaterally (JICA, JPY 6.978 tn cumulative) and through ADB (LEAP, JFPR). Run on Japan, the "foreign bank funds our infrastructure with strings" lens gives an equally or more alarming picture — tied technology on MAHSR, Japanese-funded ADB windows co-lending to Indian private companies — which nobody circulates, because the alarm is about the lender's flag, not the terms.
